---
title: "Stage 6 — execute, and get a number"
---

Running the specification against real data, in the browser.

## What this is

The analysis runs under WebR — R compiled to WebAssembly — so nothing needs installing. The
data goes in as ADaM in transport format.

**This stage assumes you have analysis datasets.** That is worth saying, because the previous
five do not. Stages 0 to 5 need a protocol and a set of definitions; this one needs subject-level
data, in the browser, in a format the engine reads.

If you have none, the chain is not wasted — the output of stage 5 is a specification complete
enough for a programmer to implement, and that is arguably the deliverable. **Executing it
proves the specification is complete; it is not what the specification is for.** A reader with a
protocol and no data can follow every stage up to here and have something real at the end of it.

If you have data but not in this shape, the work is conversion rather than authoring: collected
data standardised to SDTM, derived to ADaM, and converted to transport format. That path is not
covered here.

## What you do

**The work:** run the declared specification against real subject-level data, and keep the
record of *how* it was run — every filter and join applied — because that record, not the
number, is what the next stage needs.

1. Make the analysis data available to the engine.
2. Execute the chain.
3. Keep the execution log, not just the result.

*In the application used here:* step 8, where the datasets are loaded into the browser and the
engine starts by downloading the R runtime on first use, so it takes a moment.

### Step into the factory

Every figure above is read live from the run it came from. The runs, the chain that produced
them, and the eleven decisions taken while executing are in
`endpoints/01-simple-lab-cfb/` and `endpoints/04-vitals-cfb-mmrm/`.

## What to look out for

**Read the contrast label, never assume the direction.** The stored contrast here is placebo
minus treatment, which is the opposite of how a report would usually phrase it. Quote the
label alongside the estimate and the sign cannot be got wrong — which is exactly why this
guide prints both from the data rather than typing either.

**The engine filters on dimension names as literal columns.** Dimensions must be in their
derived forms, because the collected forms have no column in the analysis dataset. A chain
can reach stage 5 without this and fail only here.

*Check this on whatever tool you use: it is true of the application described here, at the
pinned commit, and is not a property of the concept model.*
